slot.brief: Ask for the shape and hybridisation of a xenon fluoride/oxide species (e.g. square planar XeF4-type) using lone pair counting.

stem: What are the shape and hybridisation of $text{XeF}_4$?

verdicts.working: Xe has 4 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs, giving an octahedral electron-pair arrangement and a square-planar shape; the stated hybridisation is sp³d².
issues: The XeF₄ notation contains a stray control character before “text”; the intended formula is clear.

working:
Xe has $4$ bond pairs and $2$ lone pairs.\nSteric number $= 4+2=6$; electron-pair geometry is octahedral.\nThe two lone pairs occupy opposite positions, giving square planar shape; hybridisation $sp^3d^2$.

solution:
Xe has $4$ bond pairs and $2$ lone pairs, so its steric number is $6$.
$$\text{Hybridisation}=sp^3d^2$$
The electron-pair geometry is octahedral; with lone pairs opposite each other, the molecular shape is square planar.
